                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Background\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'libGDX ships a non-rendering backend (`com.badlogicgames.gdx:gdx-backend-headless`) that swaps the live `Graphics`/`Input`/`Audio` implementations for mocks so that a libGDX `ApplicationListener` can be driven from a server, CI runner, or test harness. The bundled `MockInput` simply returns zero/`false` for every method, which makes it useless on its own for any input-driven game. A common pattern is to subclass `MockInput`, read a sequence of keystrokes from a text file, and re-dispatch them to the live `InputProcessor` each tick so that a deterministic replay of player input can drive the game from a script.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'In this task you will build a small libGDX 1.14.2 project around the **headless** backend that simulates a 2D grid walker. The walker reads a keystroke replay file, advances one keystroke per render tick by feeding it through a custom `MockInput` subclass, and prints its final position once every scripted input has been consumed.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Requirements\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Create a Gradle (Java 17) project at `/home/user/gdx-game` that depends on libGDX `1.14.2` (`gdx`, `gdx-backend-headless`, `gdx-platform:natives-desktop`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Implement a libGDX `ApplicationListener` (or `ApplicationAdapter`) that maintains a 2D integer walker position, starting at `(0, 0)`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Implement a custom `MockInput` subclass that reads a keystroke sequence from a text file and dispatches exactly one `InputProcessor.keyDown(keycode)` event per render tick. After the file is exhausted, the application must call `Gdx.app.exit()` so the headless main loop terminates cleanly.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* Drive position updates through libGDX's `InputProcessor` contract (i.e., the game must register an `InputProcessor` via `Gdx.input.setInputProcessor(...)`, and position updates happen inside that processor's callbacks).\n"[39m +
                [32m'* Produce a runnable launcher (using the Gradle `application` plugin) at `/home/user/gdx-game/build/install/gdx-game/bin/gdx-game` that accepts a `--input=<path>` argument and runs the simulation on a `HeadlessApplication`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Print the final walker position to stdout in the format `Final position: (<x>, <y>)` and exit with status code `0` on successful runs.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Input file format\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* UTF-8 text file.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* One keystroke per line. Lines are case-insensitive and trimmed of surrounding whitespace.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Blank lines are skipped (no tick is consumed).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Lines starting with `#` are treated as comments and skipped.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Allowed keystroke names: `UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`. Any other non-blank/non-comment token must cause the program to print `Error: unknown key <token>` to stderr and exit with a non-zero status code (do **not** print a `Final position:` line in that case).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Empty replay files (containing no non-blank, non-comment lines) are considered valid and must print `Final position: (0, 0)` and exit `0`.\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'### Movement semantics\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `UP` increments y by 1.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `DOWN` decrements y by 1.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `RIGHT` increments x by 1.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* `LEFT` decrements x by 1.\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Each line consumes exactly one render tick. The position update **must** happen inside the registered `InputProcessor.keyDown(int keycode)` callback (use `com.badlogic.gdx.Input.Keys.UP|DOWN|LEFT|RIGHT`).\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'## Implementation Hints\n'[39m +
                [32m'\n'[39m +
                [32m'* Pin `gdxVersion=1.14.2`. The required Maven coordinates and the headless backend recipe are summarised in the libGDX docs (https://libgdx.com/wiki/articles/dependency-management-with-gradle, https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/backends/gdx-backend-headless/src/com/badlogic/gdx/backends/headless/HeadlessApplication.java).\n'[39m +
                [32m'* The Gradle `application` plugin gives you a turnkey launcher: configure `mainClass` and run `./gradlew installDist` to produce `build/install/<projectName>/bin/<projectName>`.\n'[39m +
                [32m"* `HeadlessApplication` runs the listener on its own thread, so block the launcher's `main` thread (e.g., by joining the headless main-loop thread) until the application has exited; otherwise the JVM may quit before the simulation finishes.\n"[39m +
                [32m'* `HeadlessApplication` constructs and assigns a no-op `MockInput` to `Gdx.input` in its constructor.                     text: [32m'# TmxMapLoader throws NullPointerException when using ... - GitHub\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A help how to use the backend classes in a project · Issue #7481 · libgdx/libgdx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-20, last updated: 2025-08-07, [Read more](https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/issues/7481)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Well it depends on what you actually want to achieve, some gdx classes are regular Java objects that don't access native code nor rely on an OpenGL context being active.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'That said, if you want a regular class, just instantiate it with the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'new\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'keyword.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you need a class that relies on native code, you'll need to load the native libraries via the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SharedLibraryLoader\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m',\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"I discovery it! It's very easy actually. it's just to create in gradle(I am using a gradle project, maven should be almost same), to put a dependency:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m`implementation 'com.badlogicgames.gdx:gdx-backend-headless:1.12.1' //headless version implementation "com.badlogicgames.gdx:gdx-platform:1.12.1:natives-desktop" //necessary to have a native files\n`[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'and in our class just need to do this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'new HeadlessNativesLoader().load() Gdx.files = new HeadlessFiles()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"(I'm coding in Groovy, that's why don't have ';' at end lines) and it loads Gdx and many other files. Thanks!"[39m
                  },

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- calling a worker's method directly will wait in the main thread for it to finish.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The simplest, and probably safest way to make your program threaded is to create subclasses of QRunnable, and then run them using the QApplication's QThreadPool.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The official way to run threads in PySide is to create a subclass of\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`QtCore.QThread()`for every job.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"It's\n"[39m +
                      [32m'runmethod is designed to be overridden with your instructions to be carried out in the new thread.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'you can run it with start.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the thread is deleted before it completes (goes out of scope), your application will crash.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If storing the thread as an attribute, you should probably protect access to it with a mutex.class MyJob( QtCore.QThread ): def run(self): print('running a very long job...')\n"[39m +
                      [32m"time.sleep(5) thread = MyJob() thread.start() print('running other tasks while waiting for thread to complete')\n"[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'So i tried making the window in the class as a class variable and the command : mainloop() seems to stop everything from continuing ....As soon as you start the\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Terminal.Gui/docfx/docs/mainloop.md at v2_develop · gui-cs/Terminal.Gui\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2017-12-11, last updated: 2026-04-17, [Read more](https://github.com/gui-cs/Terminal.Gui/blob/v2_develop/docfx/docs/mainloop.md/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The method `Application.Run` will wait for events from either the keyboard or mouse and route those events to the proper view.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The job of waiting for events and dispatching them in the `Application` is implemented by an instance of the Main Loop.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This class provides the following capabilities:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Keyboard and mouse processing\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- .NET Async support\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Timers processing\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Idle processing handlers\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Invoking UI code from a background thread\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `MainLoop` property in the the `Application` provides access to these functions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When `Application.Run (Toplevel)` is called, the application will prepare the current\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`Toplevel` instance by redrawing the screen appropriately and then starting the main loop.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Configure the Mainloop before calling Application.Run, or configure the MainLoop in response to events during the execution.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'On startup, the `Application` class configures the .NET Asynchronous\n'[39m +
                      [32m'machinery to allow the use of the `await` keyword to run tasks in the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'background and have the execution of those tasks resume on the context\n'[39m +
                      [32m'of the main thread running the main loop.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Only invoke\n'[39m +
                      [32m'APIs in Terminal.Gui from the main thread by using the `Application.Invoke`'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Threading\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-24, [Read more](https://libgdx.com/wiki/app/threading)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All of the `ApplicationListener` methods are called on the same thread.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This thread is the rendering thread on which OpenGL calls can be made.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For most games it is sufficient to implement both logic updates and rendering in the `ApplicationListener.render()` method, and on the rendering thread.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Any graphics operations directly involving OpenGL need to be executed on the rendering thread.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Doing so on a different thread results in undefined behaviour.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is due to the OpenGL context only being active on the rendering thread.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Making the context current on another thread has its problems on a lot of Android devices, hence it is unsupported.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To pass data to the rendering thread from another thread we recommend using `Application.postRunnable()`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This will run the code in the Runnable in the rendering thread in the next frame, before `ApplicationListener.render()` is called.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'No class in libGDX is thread-safe unless **explicitly marked** as thread-safe in the class documentation!\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Libgdx无头应用中Mockito引发内存泄漏问题求助 - 火山引擎\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-05-22, last updated: 2026-07-02, [Read more](https://www.volcengine.com/article/680230)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'HeadlessApplication的资源与线程管理问题\n'[39m +
                      [32m'LibGDX的HeadlessApplication虽然是无头模式，但仍会启动后台线程（比如渲染循环线程），如果服务器逻辑中存在未正确释放的资源，或者线程持有对象引用导致GC无法回收，也会慢慢耗尽内存。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**解决办法：**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- 配置JVM内存参数，临时缓解问题同时帮助排查：比如增加堆内存`-Xmx2g`（根据服务器硬件调整），同时开启GC日志`-XX:+PrintGCDetails -XX:+PrintGCTimeStamps`，通过日志观察内存增长趋势，判断是内存泄漏还是正常内存占用过高。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- 检查HeadlessApplication的生命周期，确保服务器关闭或空闲时，正确调用`dispose()`清理资源。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'建议你先尝试替换Mockito的GL20 mock为手动实现的空实例，这是最快速排除潜在问题的方法。如果问题依然存在，再通过GC日志和内存分析工具定位业务逻辑或HeadlessApplication的内存泄漏点。'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Testing in libGDX with Junit on IntelliJ\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-12-21, last updated: 2025-03-24, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/77699096/testing-in-libgdx-with-junit-on-intellij)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Hi this error is due to missing an opengl context.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"So the HeadlessApplication is really to enable server side access to library stuff like Vector2 when the server/vm doesn't have a graphics context or audio, so its a kind of bypass of normal context creation as server side typically would need libGDX maths and networking but not to render anything.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"So the crash in your case is because you need an openGL context when you load the file presumably because you bind to a texture, but you don't have an openGL context in headless mode.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'The idea of headless for unit testing is that you are testing headless (i.e. non-rendering) logic.'[39m
                  }

                      [32m'created: 2012-08-10, last updated: 2025-06-15, [Read more](https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/gdx/src/com/badlogic/gdx/Application.java)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* An application can be an instance of any of the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* <ul>\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* <li>a desktop application (see <code>JglfwApplication</code> found in gdx-backends-jglfw.jar)</li>\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A help how to use the backend classes in a project · Issue #7481 · libgdx/libgdx\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-10-20, last updated: 2025-08-07, [Read more](https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/issues/7481)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'That said, if you want a regular class, just instantiate it with the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'new\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'keyword.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"If you need a class that relies on native code, you'll need to load the native libraries via the\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SharedLibraryLoader\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 使用Robot模拟左箭头按键时Gdx.input为空的初始化方法 - 火山引擎\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://www.volcengine.com/article/187831)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'如果不想引入额外的libGDX测试依赖，可以用Mockito创建一个`Input`的模拟对象，直接赋值给`Gdx.input`。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 步骤1：添加Mockito依赖\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Gradle里加：\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'testImplementation "org.mockito:mockito-core:4.+"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 步骤2：编写测试代码\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import com.badlogic.gdx.Input;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import com.badlogic.gdx.Gdx;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import static org.mockito.Mockito.mock;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import static org.mockito.Mockito.when;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'class GameScreenTest {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@Test\n'[39m +
                      [32m'void movementLeft() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 创建Input的Mock对象\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Input mockInput = mock(Input.class);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 设定当调用isKeyPressed(LEFT)时返回true\n'[39m +
                      [32m'when(mockInput.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.LEFT)).thenReturn(true);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// 把Mock对象赋值给Gdx.input\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Gdx.input = mockInput;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'int x = 10;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (Gdx.input.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.LEFT)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'x -= 5;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'assertEquals(5, x);\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A Simple Game - libGDX\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-01, [Read more](https://libgdx.com/wiki/start/a-simple-game)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'As you type `Rectangle` in IDEA, for example, it will prompt you to press alt+enter to REDACTEDcomplete the import.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Always opt for the libGDX named class in the subsequent menu.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'These are usually in the package `com.badlogic.gdx`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Open the Core project > Main.java.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This file is the main file we’re going to work in.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Declare your variables at the top of the file right underneath the `public class Main` line.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'private void input() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'float speed = .25f;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (Gdx.input.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.RIGHT)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'bucketSprite.translateX(speed); // Move the bucket right\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'private void input() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'float speed = 4f;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'float delta = Gdx.graphics.getDeltaTime();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'if (Gdx.input.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.RIGHT)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'bucketSprite.translateX(speed * delta); // move the bucket right\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (Gdx.input.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.LEFT)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'bucketSprite.translateX(-speed * delta); // move the bucket left\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'} else if (Gdx.input.isKeyPressed(Input.Keys.LEFT)) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}'[39m

                      [32m'created: 2012-08-10, last updated: 2025-01-07, [Read more](https://github.com/libgdx/libgdx/blob/master/tests/gdx-tests/src/com/badlogic/gdx/tests/InputTest.java)\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Unit Testing for user inputs - Java\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2010-11-19, last updated: 2025-03-19, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4230445/unit-testing-for-user-inputs-java)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Ideally, you'd split your input class into an interface and an implementation, and then create a MockInput for testing purposes.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'When some test needed a fake user input, you just whip up a mock one for the occasion and keep going.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The symbol and name could be hard-coded, but this way gives you some flexibility.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"You shouldn't have one class that does both, take and check user input, that's poor cohesion.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'Instead have two classes a Validator (or checker or what ever you want to call it) and an input processor that takes the user input and builds some object that the Validator understands.'[39m
                  }

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
